key_insight: PrePR-CT injects biological network knowledge as inductive priors into machine-learning models to accurately predict cell-type-specific drug responses from very limited data, yielding more interpretable and data-efficient predictions for early drug discovery.
problem_solved: Predicting how different cell types respond to drug-like compounds with scarce experimental data — a situation where standard data-hungry ML models struggle and provide limited biological interpretability.
method: Encode biological knowledge (pathways / interaction networks) as inductive priors that bias model learning toward biologically plausible patterns.
Train ML predictors that combine these priors with available drug and cell-type measurements to produce cell-type-specific response estimates in the small-data regime.
Provide interpretation by mapping model predictions back onto network components, highlighting pathways or interactions driving the predicted response.
impact: Enables ML practitioners to build more accurate, sample-efficient and interpretable models for drug-response prediction when data are scarce, accelerating early-stage screening and hypothesis generation without large-scale datasets.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: inputs (drug features, cell-type data, biological network) → prior injection → model → cell-type response predictions
Schematic diagram showing inductive priors: network nodes/edges overlay influencing model parameters
Bar/line chart comparing predictive accuracy and data efficiency of PrePR-CT vs baseline models as training set size decreases
Network heatmap or highlighted pathway graphic showing interpretable associations between network components and predicted responses
paper_title: Predicting and interpreting cell-type-specific drug responses in the small-data regime using inductive priors
paper_authors: Reem Alsulami, Robert Lehmann, Sumeer A. Khan, Vincenzo Lagani, Alberto Maillo
